title: Bunny Companion task event
description: One immutable record in a session's append-only stream. Version 2 added internalFields; the version moved because the hashed material changed, and a record is always authenticated against the rule of the version it declares so that a store written by an older build stays readable. Every event carries the hash of the one before it, which is what turns ordering, corruption detection, deduplication and safe handling of an interrupted final write into a single mechanism rather than four. The chain is unkeyed and is therefore not a defence against an attacker who can rewrite the whole file; it defends against what actually happens to a file on a constrained device. The event stream is authoritative: session and task documents are projections of it and are rebuilt from it whenever they disagree.

eventId.description: Derived from the stream position rather than minted, so it is unique within its stream by construction and identical across two runs of the same session.

taskId.description: Empty only for session_created, which is the one event type that belongs to a session rather than a task.

eventType.description: An event naming anything outside this list is refused on read rather than skipped: replaying a stream minus a record whose meaning is unknown would produce a state the machine never held. task_state_changed is the one addition to the brief's list, emitted by lifecycle moves that carry no meaning beyond the move itself, so that every transition is typed.

timestamp.description: UTC to the second. Sub-second precision in a record whose ordering is already carried by an explicit sequence number is noise that also fingerprints the machine's scheduling.

producer.description: Inside the hash, so an event cannot be re-attributed after the fact. This matters most for reviewer: an observation that could be relabelled as a runtime decision would erase the boundary the runtime exists to enforce.

payload.description: Sanitized before the event exists. Bounded at 16 KiB total, 4 KiB per string, 128 items per collection and 8 levels deep; exceeding a bound is refused rather than truncated, because a silently shortened payload reads as complete and is not.

classification.description: The class the payload warrants, never above the task's own. Events carrying the user's material take the task's class; events carrying only facts about the machine and the decision stay internal, so that a reviewer of a personal task still has something to review.

auditReference.description: Links this event to the capability plan or audit record the decision was made against.

redactions.description: Field paths removed or rewritten by sanitization. Inside the hash: the record of what was taken out is as unforgeable as the record of what was kept, and a field that vanished without trace would leave a record that reads as complete.

internalFields.description: Top-level payload keys that are runtime fact rather than the user's material, and are rendered at internal however the event as a whole is classified. Empty means none of them — every key carries the event's class, which is the safe default. Named this way round deliberately: naming the *sensitive* fields instead would be fail-open, because a payload key added later would render at internal silently. Naming what is safe to reveal means forgetting over-classifies. Inside the hash, so the list cannot be widened after the fact.

previousHash.description: The predecessor's eventHash, or sixty-four zeroes for the first event after the genesis or after a retention anchor.

eventHash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical form of every other field in this document. Nothing is outside the hash: a field outside it is a field somebody can change without the chain noticing.
